Great care must be taken to keep local governments fully informed with respect to anticipated mining plans. If good communications are maintained between the Tribal Council, the coal companies, and the Hardin and Big Horn County governments, it should be possible to develop a strategy for public facility expansion that will serve the residents of the area at reasonable cost. Breakdowns in communication could be very expensive, with the price being paid either in terms of inadequate service levels or unnecessarily high costs associated with attempts to accommodate unanticipated demand.
Education Facilities - In order to project school enrollments, two assumptions have been made: (1) only the schools in Hardin, Lodge Grass, Wyola, Fort Smith and Pryor will grow; and (2) public schools in the communities will grow in proportion to the present distribution of students in the schools' service areas. On the basis of these assumptions, it appears that all the schools face substantial enrollment increases over the 25 year study period.
The schools in Lodge Grass, Wyola, Fort Smith, Pryor and Crow Agency will be principally affected by the rise in Indian population. Therefore their enrollments are projected to rise at a steady rate (See Figure III-9) throughout the 25 year period. For details see Tables 25-28 in Appendix I. Elementary and junior high school enrollments will approximately double by 2000, but will be somewhat higher in Crow Agency and Pryor.
